description: The initial message-bus method set the Simulation Core serves (FR-M32-01 foundation). Lifecycle methods (handshake, ping, shutdown, health) are implemented; ledger and loop methods are the contract the Simulation Core fills in during Workstreams D and E.

handshake.description: First request after spawn. Carries the protocol version both ways; either side refuses on mismatch (FR-M3-08).

shutdown.description: Polite teardown request; the sidecar exits after answering (FR-M3-02).

health.description: Richer than ping: state, uptime, in-flight loop count.

attrib/blame.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C): git-native line attribution. Every line of the given paths (or all tracked files) at ref (default HEAD) mapped to (commit, author name/email, timestamp, content). Blame never lands on merge commits; renames are followed. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

attrib/diff.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C): unified-diff attribution for the working tree (default), the index (staged), or a commit range (base..compare, added lines annotated with blame attribution at compare). Renames detected; untracked files reported as added. Working-tree added lines carry commit null — there is no commit yet.

attrib/symbol.description: FR-M33-02 subset (F0 Workstream C task 14): tree-sitter line→symbol mapping — the qualified enclosing function/class of a line (e.g. "PaymentController.submit"). Unregistered languages degrade to symbol/language null, never a crash; only a missing file is an error. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

attrib/classify.description: FR-M35-02 attribution aid (F0 Workstream C task 15; gaps G3), migrated to FR-M41-04 three-state attribution (N1 Workstream B T07): deterministic human-vs-agent heuristics over working-tree/staged/range changes — burst size, multi-line insertion rate, new-file size, observed-session cross-reference. Keystroke cadence is unavailable for agents acting via file writes and is not a signal; fs/git timestamps only. Every file is labelled one of agent | human | unattributed, decided by positive evidence only — human is never 'not agent' — and every unattributed file carries the closed-vocabulary reason (FR-M41-05: no_signal | formatter_rewrite | squashed_history | pre_installation | unsupported_vendor | excluded_path) with the vocabulary version. observationConfidence telemetry|inferred (inferred is the floor, never presented as fact) with an auditable rationale. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

observe/sessions.description: FR-M35-03, X-29 (F0 Workstream D tasks 18-20): the external-agent session list behind the Crown. Sessions are detected by process inspection (vendor agent process names) and the observer framework fallback chain (OTel export, git trailers, SCM/PR API, filesystem inference), each carrying a vendor tag and observation confidence (FR-M35-02: direct/telemetry/inferred). Reads a cache refreshed by the session-monitor thread — this RPC NEVER waits on observer IO (NFR-29).

observe/health.description: FR-M35-08 (F0 Workstream D task 17): per-observer health for the External Agents screen and doctor — status ok|degraded, vendor release and adapter version (versioned observer adapters), and the sticky NFR-32 degradation warnings (format change -> visible warning, never silence).

observe/captureEvidence.description: FR-M44-12 / NFR-37 (N1 Workstream D task 21): record one volatile-evidence capture against the vendor's documented retention window (FR-M44-11). Derives capture latency (evidenceTime -> capturedAt) and the achieved margin (fraction of the window remaining; NFR-37 targets >= marginTarget under normal operation), records what was unavailable at capture time, and reports whether the capture landed inside the window. A window documented as unknown cannot report a margin (P26 — reported unknown, never invented). If the window has already closed, the response carries the explicit evidence_expired marker naming the window (FR-M44-13, AC-47) and observer health/sessions surfaces downgrade within the session.

doctor/run.description: FR-M30-01: run the self-diagnostic check registry (interpreter, sidecar, keychain/signing key, ledger integrity, git hooks, observer health). Subsystems that are not built yet report a clear not-installed status with remediation instead of failing.

ledger.append.description: Append one entry to the hash-chained ledger (FR-M10-01/02). The RPC acknowledges only after the entry and chain update are durably committed (FR-M10-08). Inputs/outputs are SEC-07-redacted and stored encrypted in the blob store (FR-M10-07); the entry references their ciphertext digests. Simulation Core entries set simulated (FR-M32-02).

ledger.query.description: Filterable entry stream (FR-M10-12, FR-M11-02): story, agent (actor), vendor, action type, sequence range, time range.

ledger.getEntry.description: FR-M11-03 entry detail: full prompt/context and output (decrypted when the caller's sidecar holds the subject key), tool calls, confidence, cost, chain hashes.

ledger.verify.description: FR-M11-01 chain integrity verdict: verified through sequence N, or a tamper indication naming the first divergent sequence (FR-M10-09).

ledger.proof.description: FR-M11-04 proof inspection: an inclusion proof for one entry, or a consistency proof between two tree sizes (RFC 6962/9162 shapes).

ledger.exportBundle.description: FR-M11-05/FR-M36-04/SEC-29/FR-M12-11 (F0 Workstream E task 25): the full signed audit bundle for any sequence range, date range, agent or story — entries with their exact hash preimages, Merkle inclusion proofs against the signed tree head, an Ed25519 signature over the whole bundle, and a compliance section mapping bundle fields to NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) provenance practice, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 record-keeping clauses and EU AI Act Article 12. Verifies standalone with the open reference verifier (FR-M36-06) using only the bundle's own public key.

hook/install.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): install the opt-in commit-msg trailer hook into the workspace repository. The hooks directory is resolved with `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, so a configured core.hooksPath is honoured. A foreign commit-msg hook is never overwritten: it is moved to commit-msg.meridian-backup and the Meridian hook chains to it (runs it first). Idempotent; one-action removal via hook/remove.

hook/status.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): report the commit-msg hook state — installed/foreign/chained, and where — so the UI and doctor show the same facts.

hook/remove.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): remove the Meridian commit-msg hook in one action, restoring a backed-up foreign hook if one was chained. Never touches a hook that is not Meridian's.

hook/pending.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 23): record a pending commit linkage — the staged-content hash (git write-tree) mapped to the ledger sequence range recorded for those changes. The commit-msg hook resolves this record at commit time and appends `Meridian-Ledger: <seq range>` to the message. Records are consumed once; a commit whose staged hash has no pending record passes through untouched.

trailers/parse.description: FR-M36-03 (F0 Workstream E task 24): agent identity trailers. Every vendor's `Co-Authored-By` variant (Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, generic `Name <email>`) in the repository's commit messages parsed into attribution records, with `Meridian-Ledger` ranges alongside; `message` parses one raw message without git. Meridian's own `Co-Authored-By: Meridian <...>` is recognised and reserved for Meridian-authored commits (meridianAuthored). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

loop.start.description: Start one of the six canonical loops (FR-M4-03).

loop.stop.description: Stop a running loop; the loop checkpoints first (FR-M4-05).

loop.status.description: Current state of a loop instance.

governance/enforcementPoints.description: FR-M42-11/12, SEC-32 (MV1-T01): every control's honest enforcement-point declaration. With no params, returns the whole registry; with `control`, that one declaration. The point comes from the closed FR-M42-11 vocabulary and the result is the EFFECTIVE declaration, not the aspirational one — an scm-point control with no SCM binding configured is reported as `sidecar` with the downgrade stated in its boundary note (D37). `enforced: false` means the control observes, records and warns; it does not intercept. No surface may render a control as enforced at a point this method does not report (SEC-32).

gate.evaluate.description: FR-M12-01/FR-M12-09 (F1 Workstream B task 9): evaluate a packet/PR payload against a named gate profile of the governance policy pack (FR-M12-01, fail-closed YAML). Every criterion is a machine-checkable DoR/DoD predicate (requiredFields, testEvidence, securityScan, humanApproval) with a pass/fail reason; the verdict is their conjunction. Fail-closed pack or unknown profile blocks. The decision is ledger-recorded (actionType gate) BEFORE the response returns (FR-M10-08).

gate.profiles.description: FR-M12-01 (F1 Workstream B task 9): list the gate profiles of the active governance policy pack — name, description, and the ordered criterion ids each profile checks. Fail-closed packs report their errors and an empty profile list.

gate.approve.description: FR-M12-05/FR-M12-07 (F1 Workstream B task 10; FR-M20-01 task 15): record a human approval for a merge subject (protected branch or PR id) bound to a commit digest. The approver identity comes from the identity provider (FR-M20-01 — git user.name/email with assurance asserted (D38) by default, OIDC stub behind the same interface), never a free-text param; anonymous approval is refused, never recorded. The full provider-resolved identity (id, displayName, email, assurance) rides the encrypted entry detail. The approval lands in the ledger (actionType approval, humanActor/humanRole set) BEFORE the RPC returns (FR-M10-08).

gate.status.description: FR-M12-05 (F1 Workstream B task 10): merge-gate status for a branch/PR subject at an optional head commit. approved only when the subject is unprotected or a recorded human approval binds the head digest; blocked carries the missing-criteria report (no approval, approval invalidated by a changed head, or an active governance halt). Read-only — decides nothing, records nothing.

gate.halt.description: FR-M12-06 (F1 Workstream B task 11): governance halts — record a halt (reason, scope: hosted-session | merge | observe-only) in the ledger before returning, then take the enforceable action available at that scope. hosted-session dispatches a gate/halt notification to the extension host's ACP session registry (the registry owns the process kill). merge enters the halted state: merge attempts for the subject (all subjects when none is named) are refused. observe-only (external agents) cannot be force-stopped (FR-M35-06 — observation never intercepts): the halt records, blocks merges, warns, and the response says exactly that (enforceable: false). Policy outranks delivery.

identity.revoke.description: FR-M42-06/SEC-31/AC-46 (N2 Workstream B task T08): record an identity revocation in the ledger (actionType identity_revocation, decision revoked, revokedAt carried). The revocation list binds from the instant the row commits: gate.approve refuses new approvals by the identity (naming revokedAt), the merge gate stops counting its approvals, and an in-flight merge authorisation bound to it is blocked at evaluation — however valid at issue. In-process effect is immediate (every check reads the ledger anew); NFR-36's five minutes is the worst-case outer envelope for OTHER replicas (e.g. an SCM-side consumer syncing the ledger), not the in-process latency. The revoking operator is the resolved human identity (FR-M20-01), attributed on the row.

gate/halt.description: Sidecar -> extension-host notification (FR-M12-06; F1 Workstream B task 11): a hosted-session halt, dispatched to the extension's ACP session registry. The registry looks up the session and owns the kill — the sidecar owns the ledger record and the dispatch, never host processes.

spend/ceiling.description: Sidecar -> extension-host notification (FR-M39-02; F1 Workstream F task 27): a spend-ceiling breach on a session Meridian hosts, dispatched to the extension's ACP session registry. The registry pauses the session at its next checkpoint — it owns the wire; the sidecar owns the ledger record (spend_ceiling entry, durable before this dispatch, FR-M10-08). Observed agents never produce this notification: they cannot be paused (FR-M35-06), and the RPC says so in its result instead.

pr/ingest.description: FR-M35-04/FR-M35-05 (F1 Workstream B task 12): ingest an external agent's PR as a Meridian story. The payload is the recorded-real gh-api pull-request shape (PR object plus its commits and files arrays — in production sourced from the M23 SCM connectors, in tests from recorded fixtures; never invented field names). The PR becomes the story's ledger origin record (actionType pr_ingest, origin connector), every hunk is attributed to its agent via Co-Authored-By trailers, author markers, or the inferred heuristic fallback (FR-M35-02 confidence labelled), each agent's pass is recorded as a proposed-change entry (actionType diff, vendor + observationConfidence set), and the packet is routed through the requested gate profiles (default verify, security, review — FR-M35-04). Every entry is written BEFORE the response returns (FR-M10-08). Merge permission is NOT granted here: pr/status consults the merge gate, which requires a recorded human approval bound to the head commit when the PR targets a protected branch (FR-M12-05, AC-32).

pr/status.description: FR-M35-04 (F1 Workstream B task 12): gate state for an ingested PR — the recorded gate evaluations for the PR's story plus the merge-gate verdict for its subject at the recorded head commit (approval required when the base branch is protected; a changed head invalidates the recorded approval). Read-only — decides nothing, records nothing.

pr/conflicts.description: FR-M35-07 (F1 Workstream B task 13): multi-agent conflict detection over a commit range. Every hunk of every non-merge commit in base..ref is attributed to its agent (Co-Authored-By trailers first, author mailbox/name markers next, human authors direct). Agent-vs-agent conflicts — a later agent's hunk whose old-side range intersects an earlier agent's new-side lines (edited or deleted the earlier agent's work), or new-side ranges intersecting (both agents added into the same region) — are surfaced as the DISTINCT rework class agent-conflict, distinct from every human-rejection reason, and recorded in the ledger (actionType rejection, reworkReason agent-conflict) before the response returns (FR-M10-08); re-runs are idempotent. Same-agent pairs are ordinary rework, never conflicts.

steer.send.description: FR-M25-01 (F1 Workstream D task 17): steer a RUNNING hosted ACP session — a human's guidance is injected into the next iteration's context over the real wire (the extension host sends a second session/prompt on the running session). The steering act is ledger-recorded BEFORE the RPC returns (FR-M10-08): who steered (the resolved human identity, FR-M20-01), what, when, into which session. Refuses with the structured NOT_HOSTED error when no hosted session_begin exists for the sessionId — an observed (not hosted) agent cannot be steered, and the refusal says so plainly (F1 Workstream D task 18). Same tier-enforcement role as gate.evaluate (governor tier, G5).

steer/question.description: FR-M25-02 (F1 Workstream D task 17): a hosted agent's clarifying question (an ACP tool-permission-style ask carrying proposed options and the agent's own recommendation in _meta) is recorded in the ledger BEFORE the human sees it — question, options, recommendation, session — so the durable question exists before any answer can (FR-M10-08). The extension host surfaces it as a blocking question; the loop resumes on answer (steer/answer). NOT_HOSTED when the session is not hosted.

steer/answer.description: FR-M25-02 (F1 Workstream D task 17): the human's answer to a recorded clarifying question. Ledger-recorded (who answered, what was chosen, linked to the question entry by sequence) BEFORE the RPC returns; the extension host then releases the answer to the waiting agent, which resumes the loop. A dismissal/cancellation is recorded honestly as a cancelled answer, never dropped. NOT_HOSTED when the session is not hosted.

steer/escalate.description: FR-M25-03 (F1 Workstream D task 17): uncertainty-triggered escalation. When a hosted agent states a confidence for an action class below the per-class threshold (the ACP _meta extension point on session/request_permission), the host records an escalation event — action class, stated confidence, threshold, session — in the ledger BEFORE the RPC returns, and surfaces it to the human (UI surface is F1 Workstream H). The policy gate asks rather than acts: the underlying action does not proceed without a recorded human decision. NOT_HOSTED when the session is not hosted.

steer/accept.description: FR-M25-04 (F1 Workstream D task 17): partial acceptance of a hosted session's output. The human accepts some files/hunks and reworks others in one action; the accepted/rejected state per file and hunk is ledger-recorded (who, when, session) BEFORE the RPC returns and is queryable via steer/acceptanceStatus. A later accept for the same session replaces the recorded state for the named files — the ledger carries the history, the status answers with the latest. NOT_HOSTED when the session is not hosted.

steer/acceptanceStatus.description: FR-M25-04 (F1 Workstream D task 17): the recorded partial-acceptance state of a hosted session's output, read back from the ledger — per file, per hunk, accepted or rejected, with the deciding human and sequence. Read-only: decides nothing, records nothing. Returns hosted: false for a session Meridian only observes (no hosted session_begin).

steer/status.description: F1 Workstream D task 18: the honest capability payload for session controls. Answers whether a session is hosted (Meridian launched and runs the ACP process) or merely observed, plus its recorded mode and lifecycle sequences. Every steer/clarify/halt control the UI renders MUST be driven by this payload's hosted flag — an observe-only session reports hosted: false so a dead control is impossible by construction. Read-only.

steer/plan.description: FR-M25-06 (F1 Workstream D task 17): dry-run planner output. In a dry-run session the agent plans and costs but writes nothing (the policy gate denies mutation kinds with the dry_run citation, recorded like any policy denial); the packet-graph plan entries and cost estimate it produced are recorded here BEFORE the RPC returns so the dry run has a durable, provable output. NOT_HOSTED when the session is not hosted.

trust.summary.description: Governor tier stub (FR-M37-*; F0 subset/F1 full): trust and rejection analytics summary. Same tier-enforcement role as gate.evaluate.

trust/detectRejections.description: FR-M37-01 subset (F0 Workstream F task 28): deterministic rejection capture from git history over base..ref (the attribution engine's diff/blame — zero model calls, FR-M36-07). A change is rejected when reverted (a later commit removes its added lines and restores its removed lines), force-amended away (its commit is unreachable and its content no longer exists at ref), or replaced within windowDays (default 7 — the meridian.rejectionWindowDays workspace setting). Each detected rejection is recorded in the ledger as an entry with actionType "rejection" carrying the rejected entry's sequence (from the commit's Meridian-Ledger trailer when present), the rejecting commit and the reason; re-running is idempotent (duplicates are skipped, never double-recorded). Detection records facts — no gate exists and none is implied.

trust/classify.description: FR-M37-06 (F0 Workstream F task 29): greenfield/brownfield classification of a story's or session's changes (a commit list or base..compare range). Greenfield when the new-file ratio is >= newFileRatioThreshold (default 0.5 — meridian.greenfieldNewFileRatio) OR the median age of the touched code is < maxMedianAgeDays (default 30 — meridian.greenfieldMaxMedianAgeDays). Deterministic from git; zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/rejectionRate.description: FR-M17-05 + FR-M37-01 (F0 Workstream F task 30, F1 Workstream E task 19): rejection rate per agent, per repository, split greenfield/brownfield (G6), derived from the ledger on demand — proposed changes are ledger entries with actionType "diff", rejections are the entries they link to via a rejection entry's rejectedSequence. Task 19 adds the FR-M37-01 scopes: phase/actionType filters, and byActionClass/byPhase/byStory views over every in-scope entry where "rejected" additionally covers entries whose own decision is rejected|reworked (rejected in review, reworked — the shapes a plain diff-link cannot see). No separate metrics database: the numbers recompute from ledger entries and cache in-process, invalidated on append. Stories are classified via trust/classify when storyCommits (storyId -> commits) and repoPath are provided; stories without commit data are reported in the unclassified bucket, never silently dropped.

trust/reasonDistribution.description: FR-M37-02 (F1 Workstream E task 20): the E-GR-03 rejection-reason distribution — every rejection entry carries a taxonomy class (reworkReason), and this reports per-class counts and rates overall, per agent (the rejected change's author, resolved through rejectedSequence), and per detection shape, split greenfield/brownfield where the stories classify (G6). Ledger-derived on demand, in-process-cached, invalidated on append (FR-M17-05). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/score.description: FR-M37-03 (F1 Workstream E task 21): the FR-M17-01 trust score per agent per task class, derived from the ledger on demand with its full decomposition exposed — first-pass yield, rejection rate, calibration error (unknown when no in-scope entry carries a confidence value — never fabricated), post-merge revert rate (the rejection detector's reverted shape over approved changes), and incident linkage (unknown: the ledger carries no incident entry type yet). A component with no evidence reports insufficient_evidence/unknown and never feeds the aggregate as zero; the aggregate covers only the components that have evidence and stays null when none do. AMD-M37 (N1 Workstream B T12): the score carries the greenfield/brownfield/unclassified split like every trust metric (storyCommits + repoPath classify through trust/classify). FR-M41-06: below the governance pack's attributionCoverageFloor the score reads insufficient_coverage and shows no value. trust/scoreDecomposition returns the identical shape under a name that reads as the decomposition-first view.

trust/scoreDecomposition.description: FR-M37-03 (F1 Workstream E task 21): alias of trust/score under the decomposition-first name — same params, same result; a bad component is visible in components, never hidden by the aggregate score.

trust/compareAgents.description: FR-M37-04 (F1 Workstream E task 22): agent-vs-agent comparison on the same story or packet (shadow mode, FR-M25-07 extended to external agents). Every agent with an in-scope entry on the story (or the actorIds list, when given) is compared side by side on first-pass yield, E-GR-03 rejection reasons, recorded cost (costUsd/tokens) and LLM ratio (the agent's share of the story's recorded token throughput). A component with no ledger evidence reports insufficient_evidence or unknown with a null value — never a fabricated zero and never a missing key. Ledger-derived on demand, in-process-cached, invalidated on append (FR-M17-05). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/jcurve.description: FR-M37-05 (F1 Workstream E task 23): the adoption J-curve — team-level throughput and stability before and after the adoption date, so the initial productivity dip DORA documents is visible as a phase rather than mistaken for failure. Throughput is the in-scope diff count per calendar week (zero-filled weeks count — the dip IS the empty weeks); stability is the F0 rejection notion (linked rejection entry or own rejected|reworked decision) before vs after. The dip is the contiguous below-baseline run of after-adoption weeks from the adoption week itself; depth is the minimum weekly throughput relative to the before-baseline. Split greenfield/brownfield/unclassified (G6) via storyCommits + repoPath as on the other trust metrics. Empty samples report insufficient_evidence, never zero. Ledger-derived on demand, in-process-cached, invalidated on append (FR-M17-05). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/tokenmaxxing.description: FR-M37-07 (F1 Workstream E task 24): tokenmaxxing detection — rising token spend without rising first-pass yield, per agent and per team. The caller supplies the spend series (spendSeries: agentId -> [{period, tokens}]; the M39 spend feed lands in a later task and this interface is deliberately vendor-agnostic); first-pass yield per period is derived from the ledger (per-period diff yield, periods matched by ISO-week labels such as 2026-W01). The detector compares the recent half of the series against the previous half: spend rise >= spendRiseThreshold (default 1.25) with a non-rising yield (mean recent yield <= previous) flags tokenmaxxing. Periods without yield evidence are excluded; an agent whose yield the ledger cannot evidence reports unknown — never flagged on fabricated numbers. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

trust/doraExport.description: FR-M37-08 (F1 Workstream E task 25): the DORA four keys — deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore — derived from the ledger and exported as OTLP-friendly JSON (resourceMetrics/scopeMetrics/metrics/gauge/dataPoints with OTel attribute encoding) so Meridian's numbers land in the team's existing engineering-intelligence tooling. Honest derivations, documented in the module: the ledger records no deploy event type, so deployments are the approved-diff shape (a change that passed review); lead time is the median hours from a story's first in-scope diff to its first approved diff; change failure is an approved diff later carried by a rejection entry; time to restore is the median hours from that failure to the story's next approved diff. A key the ledger cannot evidence exports a data point carrying meridian.evidence=unknown and NO value — never an invented number. AMD-M37 (N1 Workstream B T12): the export carries the greenfield/brownfield/unclassified split like every trust metric (storyCommits + repoPath classify through trust/classify). FR-M41-06: below the governance pack's attributionCoverageFloor every key reads insufficient_coverage and the export carries meridian.evidence=insufficient_coverage instead of a value. Python standard library only. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

spend/series.description: FR-M39-01 (F1 Workstream F task 26): the cross-vendor bill Meridian's customers cannot otherwise see — spend across every agent it observes, native and external, adapted from recorded ledger token/cost rows onto the SpendSeries protocol (D26). Aggregated by dimension: vendor | model | agent | story | team | costCentre (team/cost centre resolve through the story-metadata pack, policy/stories.yaml; dimensions with no recorded evidence report 'unknown', never fabricated). Rows with tokens but no recorded cost are priced through the pricing pack (policy/pricing.yaml) and reported as estimated, separate from recorded cost. Also returns the per-agent spendSeries (agentId -> [{period, tokens}], ISO-week periods) so trust/tokenmaxxing consumes the real feed directly. Ledger-derived on demand, in-process-cached, invalidated on append (FR-M17-05). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

spend/ceilingCheck.description: FR-M39-02 (F1 Workstream F task 27): spend ceilings from the governance pack's budgetCeilings (config, never hard-coded), enforced honestly about what Meridian controls. A hosted agent (a session Meridian launched over ACP — the session_begin record IS the hosted fact) that reaches its ceiling is recorded in the ledger (FR-M10-08: durable before any action) and a pause-at-checkpoint notification is dispatched — the extension host owns the wire and pauses the session at its next checkpoint, the same record/dispatch split as gate.halt. A Meridian-native actor (vendor 'meridian') gets the same pause-at-checkpoint dispatch for Meridian's own loops. An observed external agent gets the ADVISORY WARNING only — the same NOT_HOSTED honesty as steer: observation never intercepts (FR-M35-06), so the result says warned, never a fake pause. The warning is ledger-recorded either way.

spend/forecast.description: FR-M39-03 (F1 Workstream F task 28): monthly spend per team forecast from the trailing ledger, so the bill is visible before it arrives. Method (documented, deterministic): an ordinary least-squares line over the trailing windowMonths calendar months (default 3; zero months included — a month with no recorded token activity is real evidence of no spend), evaluated at the current month; fewer than two evidence months reports insufficient_evidence, never a projection on one point. Budget alert: when the month-to-date actual or the projection crosses budgetCeilings.usdPerMonth from the governance pack (config, never hard-coded) the status is actual_breach | forecast_breach | ok; no configured budget reports unconfigured and the forecast is still returned. The team dimension resolves through the story-metadata pack; unmapped stories are excluded and counted, never silently attributed. Ledger-derived on demand, in-process-cached, invalidated on append (FR-M17-05). Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

spend/pricing.description: FR-M39-04 (F1 Workstream F task 29): the pricing table that makes spend predictable — per-vendor/model token rates (USD per million tokens, USD default per D12, currency configurable) from the pricing pack (policy/pricing.yaml, workspace override at .meridian/policy/pricing.yaml; all rates from config, never hard-coded). Recorded tokens x rate = cost wherever the ledger recorded tokens without cost; a model with no rate prices as unknown, never a fabricated number. Meridian's own pricing model is predictable by design: the Flight Recorder tier makes no model calls and has no usage-based cost (meridian rates are 0.0); the Governor and Orchestra tiers report their own model spend in the same ledger as everyone else's. Fail-closed parsing like the governance pack: a malformed pack prices nothing. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

acp/sessionBegin.description: FR-M34-01/02 (F1 Workstream A task 4): the extension host ACP client reports a hosted agent session starting; the sidecar records a `session_begin` ledger entry (actorKind external, vendor acp, direct confidence) before the agent's first turn.

acp/sessionEnd.description: FR-M34-01/02 (F1 Workstream A task 4): the extension host reports a hosted session ending (stop reason, timing); the sidecar records a `session_end` ledger entry, attributing it to the same actor as the session's begin entry.

acp/permissionDecision.description: FR-M34-04/SEC-28 (F1 Workstream A task 4): records one ACP permission decision — selected option, cancellation, policy denial (outcome denied_by_policy, reason cited) or a SEC-28 re-request auto-denial — as a `permission_decision` ledger entry so the governance trail is durable before and independently of the human answer.

worktree/create.description: FR-M18-01/02/05/07 (F1 Workstream A task 5): create the story worktree for a hosted agent — a linked git worktree under <repo>/.meridian/worktrees/<story-id>/ on branch meridian/<story-id> (configurable via baseBranch) forked from the base branch, with a worktree-local agent git identity derived from the adapter id and a worktree-local commit-msg hook appending the Meridian-Hosted-Agent trailer to every commit the agent makes. The primary working tree is NEVER the write target. Ledger-recorded (action_type worktree_create, worktree_ref set).

worktree/list.description: FR-M18-01 (F1 Workstream A task 5): the Meridian-managed story worktrees of this repository (those under .meridian/worktrees/), each with branch, base and head. Read-only; consumed by the open-in-window command (FR-M18-08) among others.

worktree/remove.description: FR-M18-01 (F1 Workstream A task 5): remove a story worktree (git worktree remove; refuses when the worktree is dirty unless force). The branch is NOT deleted here — that is story abort (worktree/abortStory) or post-merge GC (FR-M18-09). Ledger-recorded (action_type worktree_remove, worktree_ref set).

worktree/abortStory.description: FR-M18-04 (F1 Workstream A task 5): story abort — remove the story worktree, delete the story branch when it has never been pushed (a pushed branch is kept and branchKeptReason says why), and ledger-record the abort (action_type story_abort, worktree_ref set). The primary working tree is left byte-identical (AC-14).

worktree/conflicts.description: FR-M18-03 (F1 Workstream A task 5, AC-13): pre-flight conflict detection before a packet starts — divergence between the story branch and the base branch (unmerged upstream changes), uncommitted changes in the primary tree colliding with the packet's target paths (all dirty files reported when targetPaths is absent), and uncommitted/unpushed state in the story worktree itself. Returns a structured report; blocked=true means the run must not start. The RunRequest/preflight flow (M40, gaps_initiation §7.11) consumes this report.

mcp/invoke.description: FR-M34-06 (F1 Workstream A task 6): the MCP server gateway. The standalone MCP server process (extension/src/mcp/, governor tier) forwards every MCP tools/call as one mcp/invoke; the sidecar's tier gate is the permission gate (governor disabled => TIER_DISABLED, G5), the call is ledger-recorded as a `tool_call` entry (vendor mcp, direct confidence) BEFORE it runs, and the named tool maps onto the existing read-only handler — ledger_query -> ledger.query, ledger_export_bundle -> ledger.exportBundle, ledger_verify -> ledger.verify, trust_rejection_rate -> trust/rejectionRate. Unknown tool names are refused with INVALID_PARAMS listing the available tools; the underlying result passes through verbatim.

roles/list.description: FR-M20-02 (F1 Workstream C task 16): the active role pack — the FR-M20-02 roles (Engineer, Reviewer, Approver, Governor, Auditor), each with its permitted gate actions and read-only flag, plus the approval mechanics configuration: N-of-M thresholds per protected branch (FR-M20-04), the separation-of-duties flag (FR-M20-03), delegation bounds (FR-M20-05) and the approval-hygiene thresholds (FR-M20-06). Fail-closed packs report their errors and an empty role list.

roles/check.description: FR-M20-02/07/08 (F1 Workstream C task 16): may `role` perform `action` (approve | halt | policy-change | delegate | export-audit)? Returns a structured {permitted, reason}; the reason names the permitted roles on refusal — only Governor may policy-change (FR-M20-07), Auditor is read-only and holds only export-audit (FR-M20-08). A fail-closed roles policy refuses every check with the parse errors as the reason.

roles/delegate.description: FR-M20-05 (F1 Workstream C task 16): delegate an approval right to another principal with expiry. The delegator is the acting provider-resolved identity (FR-M20-01) and must hold the right by role or through an active delegation chain; chains are depth-bounded (delegation.maxChainDepth) and cycles are refused. The delegation is ledger-recorded (actionType delegation, from/to/role/expiresAt/depth in the encrypted detail) BEFORE the response returns (FR-M10-08); expiry is enforced at approval time — an expired delegation grants nothing.

tiers/set.description: FR-M36-05: notification carrying the enabled tier set after a meridian.tiers configuration change, so a tier flip needs no reinstall and no window reload. The base tier (flight-recorder) is always enabled regardless of payload.

$/cancel.description: Notification cancelling an in-flight request by id (FR-M1-09).

evidence/gate.description: F2 (gaps_implementation.md §F2): the evidence gate computed rather than argued. Twenty real stories through F0+F1 produce a GO / STOP / PIVOT / KILL with the measures behind it, from the ledger's own record. Every measure that cannot be evidenced reads unavailable with the reason, never zero; a verdict over fewer than twenty stories is insufficient_evidence. The exit criterion is a written decision with the raw ledger slice attached, and this is the computed half of it. Zero model calls (FR-M36-07).

CoverageEnvelope.description: FR-M41-08 (N1 Workstream A, D36): the coverage disclosure every analytic result carries — computed in the same operation as the figure, never a separate call (NFR-34). G-01's defect was silent 1,000-row truncation; the envelope makes any residual bound visible. trust/score carries it under `coverageEnvelope` because that result's `coverage` key already names the FR-M37-03 component list.

value.description: The headline figure the envelope qualifies; null for a multi-figure result or when the metric itself reads insufficient_evidence.

rowsConsidered.description: Rows of the figure's population the metric actually examined.

rowsAvailable.description: Rows the ledger holds in the metric's declared scope (a caller-declared fromSequence/toSequence window is the available population — a declared window is not truncation).

truncated.description: True when any scan stopped short of its available population (the old 1,000-row clamp). FR-M41-09: surfaces must state this in text and disable derived projections when true.

sequenceRange.description: The inclusive [first, last] ledger sequences the figure covered; [null, null] over an empty sample.

coverage.description: The explicit ratio rowsConsidered / rowsAvailable (1.0 over an empty available population).

label.description: complete: nothing missed; partial: some of the available population unseen; empty: nothing available.

attribution.description: FR-M41-06: the attribution-coverage dimension of the figure's population (three-state counts, the attributed share, the configured floor and whether it was breached); null on surfaces that do not attribute their population.

AttributionCoverage.description: FR-M41-06 (N1 Workstream B T09): the attribution-coverage dimension every trust metric reports — how much of the metric's population is positively attributable. Below the configured floor the metric reads insufficient_coverage and shows no value (P25: a metric over a population it cannot attribute is not evidence).

agent.description: Rows positively attributed to an agent (FR-M41-04).

human.description: Rows positively attributed to a human (FR-M41-04).

unattributed.description: Rows with no positive authorship evidence — reported, never absorbed into agent or human (P26).

coverage.description: The attributed share (agent + human) / population; 1.0 over an empty population (whose verdict is the metric's own insufficient_evidence).

floor.description: The configured policy floor (governance pack attributionCoverageFloor); null = unconfigured, no suppression.

belowFloor.description: True when the attributed share fell below the floor over a non-empty population — the metric reads insufficient_coverage and shows no value.

protocolVersion.description: Must equal PROTOCOL_VERSION or the sidecar refuses with PROTOCOL_MISMATCH.

tiers.description: FR-M36-05: tiers enabled in this workspace (from the meridian.tiers setting). Absent means the sidecar default: flight-recorder only. The base tier is always enabled regardless.

workspaceDir.description: Absolute workspace path. The ledger lives at <workspaceDir>/.meridian/ledger (FR-M10-01). Absent: ledger RPCs answer LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE until configured.

ledgerSigningKey.description: Base64-encoded 32-byte Ed25519 seed (FR-M10-04), sourced from the extension host's OS-keychain-backed SecretStorage (SEC-06) and provisioned over this handshake. Held in memory only; never persisted to disk or written into the ledger. Absent: the sidecar signs tree heads with an ephemeral key and doctor reports the missing keychain key.

identityProvider.description: FR-M20-01 (D9; F1 Workstream C task 15): selects the human identity source — "git" (default; user.name/user.email in the workspace, assurance asserted per D38) or "oidc" (enterprise OIDC; contracted stub raising NOT_IMPLEMENTED with the FR id until the enterprise tier lands). Selected over the handshake like the ledger signing key: the extension host owns the choice it can later back with SecretStorage OIDC tokens. Unknown names are refused with an actionable INVALID_PARAMS. Requires workspaceDir.

policyScaffolds.description: D43/AC-53 (N0-T09b): the policy-bootstrap events from the workspace handshake — one per sidecar-loaded policy pack. action 'scaffolded' means the shipped default was copied into <ws>/.meridian/policy/ on first run (the host surfaces these as the visible first-run notice); 'present' means the workspace pack won and nothing was copied; 'missing-default' names a broken install.

DoctorCheckStatus.description: Outcome of one doctor check. warn means usable but degraded or not yet installed; fail means broken and actionable.

id.description: Stable machine id, e.g. interpreter, sidecar, ledger.

detail.description: What was found, in one line.

remediation.description: Actionable fix; always present on warn and fail.

checks.description: Subset of check ids to run; absent runs the whole registry.

workspaceDir.description: Absolute path of the workspace folder; the git-hooks check needs it.

status.description: Worst status across all checks: fail > warn > pass.

repoPath.description: Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

paths.description: Worktree-relative file filter; absent blames every tracked file.

line.description: 1-based line number in the ref's version of the file.

commit.description: Full hex sha of the introducing commit; never a merge commit.

content.description: Line content without the terminator (CRLF tolerated).

repoPath.description: Resolved repository toplevel.

provenance.description: FR-M41-01/02: per-field provenance — each field carries source, captureMethod, contractVersion, capturedAt and state (observed here: every blame field is read directly from git, nothing inferred).

ProvenanceField.description: FR-M41-01/02 (N1 Workstream B T10): one field of a provenance answer with its full evidence chain. state is one of exactly observed | inferred | unknown | redacted; signing an artefact never promotes inferred to observed (the state is inside the signed bytes).

value.description: The field's content; null when the state is unknown or redacted — never invented.

source.description: Where the fact came from: git, the symbols engine, rpc params, the heuristic classifier, ...

captureMethod.description: How it was captured: porcelain parse, tree-sitter walk, burst/timing heuristics, ...

contractVersion.description: The version of the contract that produced the field (attrib-provenance/v1).

state.description: observed: read directly from evidence; inferred: derived by a documented deterministic rule (signing never promotes it); unknown: no evidence exists; redacted: withheld by policy.

repoPath.description: Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

base.description: Range start (commit-ish). With compare: base..compare; alone: base vs worktree.

compare.description: Range end (commit-ish); added lines are blame-annotated at this ref.

staged.description: Diff the index against HEAD (base optionally overrides HEAD).

oldLine.description: 1-based in the base version; null for pure additions.

newLine.description: 1-based in the compare version; null for removals.

commit.description: Introducing commit for range-diff added lines (blame at compare); null for worktree/index changes.

repoPath.description: Resolved repository toplevel.
Absolute path of the git repository (any directory inside it is accepted and resolved to the toplevel).

language.description: Registered language id; null when the extension is not registered.

symbol.description: Qualified enclosing definition, e.g. PaymentController.submit; null when none or degraded.

provenance.description: FR-M41-01/02: per-field provenance. language/symbol are observed when resolved and honestly unknown (never inferred) when null — G3 degradation never overclaims.

AttribObservedSession.description: An externally observed agent session (Workstream D supplies these; the heuristic only consumes them). Its presence covering an edit window raises the agent attribution weight and lifts the label to telemetry.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 or epoch seconds; absent means currently active. A file edited before this time is not covered.

excludedPaths.description: FR-M41-05: paths excluded from attribution (exact, directory prefix, or glob). Matching files report unattributed/excluded_path — excluded is reported, never silently dropped.

AttribAttribution.description: FR-M41-04: exactly three mutually exclusive states — agent | human | unattributed — decided by positive evidence only; no state is ever derived by subtracting the others (human is never 'not agent'). unattributed is a first-class honest answer (G3, P26).

AttribUnknownReason.description: FR-M41-05: the closed, versioned vocabulary of reasons an unattributed span could not be resolved. Recorded with every classification as unknownReason + unknownReasonVersion.

burstLines.description: Lines added in the same timestamp sweep / commit as this file's edits.

multiLineInsertRate.description: Fraction of insertion hunks adding >=5 lines at once.

editTimestamp.description: Filesystem mtime of the edited file, ISO 8601 UTC; null for deletes.

unknownReason.description: FR-M41-05: the closed-vocabulary reason when attribution is unattributed; null on agent/human spans.

unknownReasonVersion.description: The version of the unknown-reason vocabulary this answer was produced under (FR-M41-05).

observationConfidence.description: FR-M35-02; heuristic output is never better than telemetry and the floor is inferred.

rationale.description: Human-readable signals behind the weight, for UI disclosure.

LedgerAppendParams.description: One ledger entry, §7.2 columns in camelCase. input/output are redacted (SEC-07), encrypted and content-addressed (FR-M10-07); blob_subject selects the per-subject key (FR-M10-14).

input.description: Full prompt/context; redacted + encrypted into the blob store.

output.description: Resulting output; redacted + encrypted into the blob store.

vendor.description: Default 'meridian'; external agents carry their vendor (FR-M35-03).

origin.description: FR-M40-02: written with the run's first entry.

simulated.description: FR-M32-02 simulation marker; absent means false.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC override (replay/golden corpus); absent = now.

blobSubject.description: Subject for the per-subject blob key; default 'default'.

hash.description: entry_hash hex, chained from the previous (FR-M10-02).

treeHead.description: Present when this append emitted a signed tree head (FR-M10-04).

TreeHead.description: FR-M10-04 signed tree head: the Merkle root over entries 1..seq, Ed25519-signed; hex-encoded.

limit.description: Page size, default 100, clamped to 1000 (FR-M41-07: a page size, never the only bound — page the full history with afterSequence).

afterSequence.description: FR-M41-07 cursor (exclusive): rows with seq > afterSequence, ascending. Feed the last returned row's sequence back in until a page comes back short.

LedgerEntry.description: FR-M11-02 stream shape: one ledger entry with chain hashes; blob payloads are referenced by digest/ref, not inlined.

toolCallsSummary.description: Count of tool calls; the array itself is in the entry detail (FR-M11-03).

rejectedSequence.description: FR-M37-01: on actionType "rejection" entries — the rejected entry's ledger sequence.

rejectedCommit.description: FR-M37-01: on rejection entries — the commit whose change was rejected.

rejectingCommit.description: FR-M37-01: on rejection entries — the commit that rejected it (null for force_amended).

truncated.description: FR-M41-07: true when the page hit its size limit while more rows match — the clamp is reported, never silent. Page with afterSequence; the envelope-carrying metrics never set this.

nextAfterSequence.description: The cursor for the next page: the last returned row's sequence (null when entries is empty). Feed it back as afterSequence.

LedgerGetEntryResult.description: FR-M11-03 detail. input/output carry the decrypted blob text when the sidecar holds the subject key; *Available flags say whether decryption succeeded (false when the key was crypto-shredded).

upTo.description: Verify a prefix only; absent verifies the whole chain.

LedgerInclusionProof.description: RFC 6962 audit path for one leaf; hex-encoded hashes, leaf-upwards order (verifier: RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2).

LedgerConsistencyProof.description: RFC 6962/9162 consistency proof between two tree sizes; hex-encoded hashes (verifier: RFC 9162 §2.1.4.2).

fromSize.description: Consistency proof: the earlier tree size.

toSize.description: Consistency proof: the later tree size.

fromTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 lower bound on entry timestamps (with the sequence range).

toTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 upper bound on entry timestamps (with the sequence range).

LedgerBundleEntry.description: One entry in an audit bundle: the FR-M11-02 stream shape plus ciphertext refs and digests, so a third-party verifier can check the chain segment without any key. `hashPayload` is the exact JSON-native preimage of the entry hash (ledger columns minus entryHash/previousHash, digests hex-projected) — the open verifier hashes it byte-for-byte per the canonical JSON rules; it is the anchor of truth, the sibling fields are the human-readable view.

hashPayload.description: The exact preimage of entryHash per the open ledger spec: ledger_entry columns minus entryHash/previousHash, byte digests hex-projected, JSON-native values.

publicKey.description: Base64 raw public key; signature verification needs no trust in Meridian servers (SEC-29).

LedgerBundleInclusion.description: RFC 6962 §2.1.1 audit path proving one entry's leaf (its entryHash) is included in the Merkle tree the signed tree head commits to.

sequence.description: The ledger sequence this proof is for (1-based; the leaf index is sequence - 1).

LedgerBundleProofs.description: Merkle proofs for every included entry, against the tree size and root the signed tree head commits to (FR-M36-04/SEC-29: the bundle verifies standalone).

LedgerBundleSignature.description: Ed25519 signature over the whole bundle (FR-M36-04): `digest` is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the entire bundle object minus this signature block; the signature signs the 32 digest bytes with the ledger key. Verification needs only the bundled public key (SEC-29).

digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the canonical bundle core (bundle minus this block).

signature.description: Hex Ed25519 signature over the raw 32 digest bytes.

LedgerComplianceMapping.description: One mapping from a bundle field set to a record-keeping requirement (FR-M12-11 as amended by gaps-requirements M12: NIST SSDF AI provenance + ISO/IEC 42001 + EU AI Act Article 12).

LedgerComplianceSection.description: The compliance section: which standards the bundle maps to and every field-level mapping (FR-M36-04, FR-M12-11).

formatVersion.description: Bundle format v1; pinned by the open ledger spec (FR-M36-06, docs/open-ledger-spec/).

treeHead.description: Signed head covering the ledger tip at export time; absent only when the ledger has no entries yet.

workspaceDir.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

chained.description: True when a foreign commit-msg hook was backed up and is invoked by the Meridian hook before its own trailer logic.

alreadyInstalled.description: True when the hook was already Meridian's — install is idempotent.

installed.description: A commit-msg hook exists and carries the Meridian marker.

foreignHook.description: A commit-msg hook exists that is NOT Meridian's — it is left untouched.

removed.description: False when there was no Meridian hook to remove; the repository is left untouched.

restoredBackup.description: True when a chained foreign hook was restored to commit-msg.

stagedHash.description: The staged-content key: the hex of the tree object git write-tree produces for the index (`git write-tree`).

TrailerAttribution.description: One Co-Authored-By trailer value as an attribution record (FR-M36-03, task 24): the claimed identity, the vendor it resolves to (claude | github-copilot | cursor | generic | meridian | unknown), and whether this is Meridian's own reserved co-author line.

TrailerCommit.description: One commit's trailer facts: its agent attributions and the Meridian-Ledger sequence ranges it carries. `commit`/`authoredAt` are null only for the direct-message parse path.

repoPath.description: Repository root. Absent means the handshake workspaceDir.

ref.description: Range or rev to walk, default HEAD. Any git log ref grammar (e.g. a..b).

since.description: ISO-8601 cutoff; only commits at or after it are parsed.

message.description: Parse this raw commit message directly — no repository needed; returns a single synthetic commit.

lastCheckpoint.description: Durable checkpoint id (FR-M4-05), present once the loop has checkpointed.

gate.description: Gate profile name from the policy pack (FR-M12-01), e.g. ready, verify, security, review.

packet.description: The packet/PR payload the criteria check: fields (storyId, branch, headCommit...), evidence artifacts (kind/status/criticalFindings), approvals. Free-form; criteria address it by key.

policyPath.description: Optional explicit policy pack path; defaults to the workspace override then the repository policy directory.

policyVersion.description: governance/v<N> of the pack that decided; governance/invalid on a fail-closed pack.

failClosed.description: True when the active pack failed closed (malformed/missing policy) — every evaluation blocks.

reasons.description: One reason per failed criterion (plus policy errors when fail-closed).

control.description: One control id. Omit for the whole registry. An unknown id is an error, never an empty result — a control nobody declared is a bug, not an absence (P26).

scmBindingConfigured.description: Whether an SCM-native check is configured for this workspace. Default false, which is v1's reality (D37): with no binding, scm-point controls report their effective sidecar point instead.

vocabularyVersion.description: Bumped whenever the vocabulary or a declaration's semantics change, so a recorded declaration stays interpretable without this build.

controls.description: Control id to its effective declaration.

enforcementPoint.description: Where the control ACTUALLY binds, after any D37 downgrade.

enforced.description: false = advisory: it observes, records and warns, and no surface may render it as enforced (SEC-32).

boundaryNote.description: What could bypass this control and who could do so. Written to be quoted into an audit bundle verbatim (FR-M42-12).

criteria.description: Ordered criterion ids the profile checks.

subject.description: The merge subject: protected branch name or PR id.

commit.description: Head commit digest the approval binds. A changed head invalidates the approval.

role.description: The approver's role (checked against the role pack, FR-M20-02; absent uses the pack's defaultRole).

rolePath.description: FR-M20-02: role pack override for the permission, SoD and N-of-M checks.

ApprovedBy.description: FR-M42-07 (N1-T18, decision D40): the closed, versioned approval-classification block every approval and permission decision carries. class is Meridian-owned closed vocabulary v1: human_individual | human_delegated | bot_agent | ruleset_actor | unknown; classifierVersion is the vocabulary version (approvedBy/v1) that produced the class. A non-human class (bot_agent | ruleset_actor | unknown) NEVER satisfies a human-approval policy and never counts as a human approval in any metric (FR-M42-08, AC-44). FR-M42-04/06 (D38, N2-T08): identityAssurance is the D38 assurance level (asserted | verified) the acting human resolved at, bound to the decision; absent on non-human classes and pre-N2 rows — never fabricated, never a silent upgrade to verified.

identityAssurance.description: FR-M42-04/06: the identity assurance level bound to this human decision (asserted = git self-asserted, D38; verified = OIDC-attested). "unrecorded" names a human decision whose identity could not be resolved at capture — honest, never a silent verified.

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the approval entry — durable before this response returns.

approvedBy.description: FR-M42-07: the stamped approval class — human_individual as themselves, human_delegated when an active delegation grant (FR-M20-05) carried the approve permission.

commit.description: Current head digest; an approval bound to a different digest is invalidated.

rolePath.description: FR-M20-02/04/06: role pack override for the N-of-M count and hygiene warnings.

requiredApproval.description: True when the subject is a protected branch.

halted.description: True when an active governance halt blocks this subject.

approvalSequence.description: The bound approval's ledger sequence; present only when approved via an approval.

requiredApprovals.description: FR-M20-04: distinct recorded approvers required (the N-of-M threshold; 1 unless the role pack names the subject's branch).

approvalsReceived.description: FR-M20-04: how many distinct approvers' valid approvals the ledger currently holds for this subject.

approvedBy.description: FR-M42-07: the bound approval's class; absent when blocked. Approvals with a non-human class never bind and never enter this count (FR-M42-08, AC-44).

hygieneWarnings.description: FR-M20-06: advisory rubber-stamping signals measured from ledger history — sub-threshold approve latency, approver == requester, back-to-back bulk approvals. The F2 measurement hook; never changes the verdict.

reason.description: Why governance halted; recorded in the ledger and quoted in the merge-gate report.

subject.description: Branch/PR the halt binds; absent = global (every subject).

sessionId.description: Required for scope hosted-session: the ACP session to terminate.

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the halt entry — durable before this response returns.

enforceable.description: False exactly when the scope cannot be force-stopped (observe-only, FR-M35-06).

warning.description: Present when the halt could not be fully enforced (observe-only): says exactly what did and did not happen.

email.description: The identity (email) to revoke — the lookup key every governance check uses.

reason.description: Why governance revoked the identity; recorded in the ledger.

revokedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC — the provider-side instant the revocation took effect; defaults to now. In-process enforcement binds from row commit (immediate), whatever timestamp is carried.

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the identity_revocation row — durable before this response returns (FR-M10-08), and binding from this instant in-process (NFR-36/AC-46).

action.description: terminated = dispatched to the session registry; blocked = merge gate halted; warned = operator warned, agent untouched.

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the halt entry.

rolePath.description: Explicit role pack path override; absent resolves .meridian/policy/roles.yaml then policy/roles.yaml under the workspace, then the built-in default.

permissions.description: The gate actions this role may perform (FR-M20-02 mapping).

readOnly.description: True for the Auditor: read-only across the ledger (FR-M20-08).

nOfM.description: FR-M20-04: protected branch -> required count of distinct approvers.

defaultRole.description: The role gate.approve checks when the caller passes no explicit role; absent on a fail-closed pack.

reason.description: On refusal, names the rule and the permitted roles.

to.description: The principal receiving the right (email or named holder).

role.description: The approval right being delegated; must hold the approve permission.

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC expiry. Absent: computed from ttlDays.

ttlDays.description: TTL in days when expiresAt is absent; must be <= delegation.maxTtlDays.

holderRole.description: The role the delegator holds (validated against the pack). Absent: the delegator must hold via an active delegation chain.

depth.description: 1 = direct grant from a role holder; each re-delegation adds one.

sequence.description: Ledger sequence of the delegation entry — durable before this response returns.

sessionId.description: The hosted ACP session being steered. Must have a recorded session_begin; otherwise the structured NOT_HOSTED refusal.

message.description: The human's guidance, injected into the running session's next iteration context.

agentId.description: "<vendor>:<login>" — the ledger actor_id for this agent.

confidence.description: FR-M35-02 observation confidence for the attribution evidence (trailer/author-marker evidence is telemetry; the heuristic fallback is always inferred).

rationale.description: Auditable why: which evidence attributed this hunk, and any ambiguity (multi-agent PRs degrade to inferred rather than overclaiming, G3).

sequence.description: The ledger sequence of the recorded gate evaluation (FR-M10-08 — written before the response returns).

pr.description: The gh-api pull-request payload: the PR object plus its commits (list-commits-for-a-pull shape) and files (list-files shape with per-file patch). Recorded-real field names only.

linkedTicket.description: The ticket the PR closes (Jira-style ticket key). Absent: derived from the body/title/branch (the ticket-to-PR flow, FR-M35-05); the PR subject is the story id when no key is found.

gates.description: Gate profile chain to route the packet through (default [verify, security, review]).

evidence.description: Check-run/scan artifacts for the gate criteria (kind/status/criticalFindings), gh-api check-runs shaped.

approvals.description: Review approvals for the humanApproval criterion (approver name/email, role), gh-api reviews shaped.
